slides.eyebrow: This mistake costs more than you think
slides.sub: On a conventional loan, PMI doesn't last forever. Here's when it can come off.

slides.title: PMI protects the lender
slides.body: Private mortgage insurance protects the lender, not you. On a conventional loan, you'll usually pay it if you put down less than 20%.
slides.source: CFPB, What is private mortgage insurance? (Oct. 2026)

slides.label: You can ask to cancel at
slides.body: Ask in writing once your balance hits or is scheduled to hit 80% of the original value. You'll need on-time payments, no second mortgage and proof the value hasn't dropped.
slides.source: CFPB, When can I remove PMI from my loan? (Oct. 2026)

slides.label: It ends on its own at
slides.body: Your servicer has to end PMI once your balance is scheduled to reach 78% of the original value, as long as you're current.
slides.source: CFPB, When can I remove PMI from my loan? (Oct. 2026)

slides.title: FHA and VA are different
slides.body: These rules are for conventional loans. FHA and VA loans have different rules, so ask your servicer how yours works. Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
slides.source: CFPB, When can I remove PMI from my loan? (Oct. 2026)

caption:
Paying PMI longer than you have to is a mistake that costs more than you think.

PMI protects the lender, not you. On a conventional loan, you can ask in writing to cancel it once your balance hits or is scheduled to hit 80% of the home's original value. You'll need on-time payments, no second mortgage and proof the value hasn't dropped. Your servicer has to end it once your balance is scheduled to reach 78%, as long as you're current. FHA and VA loans have different rules.

Talk to a licensed lender for your numbers.
